rule: published artifacts stay byte-identical; corrections are appended

entries.source_section_or_line: GAMMA_FIT = (10, 1000) -- the fit range, never swept
entries.old_statement: gamma = 0.407 / 0.379 / 0.411 (200 ms merge), treated as the exponent
entries.corrected_statement: gamma depends strongly on the FIT RANGE, which no run in this lane ever swept. Fitting the same C(l) over [5, 200] instead of [10, 1000] gives 0.795 (BTC) and 0.729 (ETH) against 0.407 and 0.379 -- roughly DOUBLE -- while SOL barely moves (0.407 vs 0.411). A pure power law would give the same exponent on any range, so the real C(l) is not one. Second independent reason for GAMMA_IS_NOT_A_SINGLE_NUMBER (C-T25 found the first: it depends on which variable's autocorrelation is taken). C-T28's recovery calibrated at ONE fixed range, so it measured precision, not range-robustness.

entries.old_statement: the composite is rejected on BTC (z -2.51) and SOL (z -3.15), with the measured kappa-chi BELOW the prediction
entries.corrected_statement: The prediction used gamma from the [10, 1000] fit range. With [5, 200] gamma is 0.795 on BTC, so (1-gamma)/2 = 0.103 against a measured kappa-chi of 0.2245 -- a rejection in the OPPOSITE direction. The verdict's SIGN is range-dependent. The rejection is not withdrawn (both ranges reject) but its DIRECTION, and any story about beta being below or above beta_c, is NOT ESTABLISHED.

entries.old_statement: MO_only gamma reported as 0.795 / 0.729 / 0.407 alongside C-T19's 0.407 / 0.379 / 0.411
entries.corrected_statement: This run's MO_only contains only market orders that MOVED the mid, while C-T19's gamma was measured on ALL market orders. Two different populations printed side by side as if comparable. Part of the gap is the fit range (ERR-HU-032) and part is this; the run does not separate them.
